Pigmentation & Melasma Treatment in Jaipur | Fading Dark Patches Safely

Pigmentation treatment fades dark patches, marks and spots by treating what causes them. For melasma, acne marks and sun spots, that usually means daily sun protection, prescription creams and, when needed, chemical peels or laser toning, planned for your skin type. At Kezza, pigmentation is assessed and treated by our doctors at our Jaipur, Sikar and Ajmer clinics.

The Condition

What Is Pigmentation, and What Is Melasma?

Pigmentation means patches or spots of skin that are darker than the rest. Melasma is one common type: brown or grey-brown patches on the cheeks, forehead, nose or upper lip, triggered by sun, heat and hormones. It can be controlled with sun protection and treatment, but it often returns, so care continues after it fades.

Skin colour comes from melanin. When the skin makes too much of it in one place, a dark patch appears. Melasma is most common in women with medium to dark skin and usually starts between the ages of 20 and 40. Sunlight, visible light, heat, pregnancy, contraceptive pills and family history can all trigger or worsen it, and it often looks symmetrical on both cheeks.

Other kinds of pigmentation look different and are treated differently. Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation is the dark mark left after a pimple, eczema, a burn or an injury, and it is more common in darker skin. Sun spots are flat brown spots on skin that gets a lot of sun and, unlike freckles, they do not fade in winter. Tanning is the skin's response to ultraviolet light and is itself a sign of sun damage.

Because each type has a different cause, the first step is working out which kind you have. A spot that is new, changing, itching or bleeding is checked by a doctor before any cosmetic treatment, because a small number of dark spots are not pigmentation at all.

In Short:

  • Find the cause: melasma, marks, sun spots or tan.
  • Protect daily: sunscreen is part of every plan.
  • Be patient: results build over months, not days.
What We Treat

Types of Pigmentation We Treat

Melasma

Symmetrical brown or grey-brown patches on the cheeks, forehead, nose or upper lip, often linked to sun, heat or hormones.

Marks After Acne

Flat dark marks left after pimples heal. They are not scars and usually fade faster with sun protection and treatment.

Sun Spots

Flat brown spots on the face, hands and arms from years of sun exposure that do not fade in winter.

Tanning & Uneven Tone

Patchy darkening on sun-exposed skin, such as the face, neck and forearms.

Freckles

Small light-brown spots that darken in summer. They are harmless, and treatment is a personal choice.

Marks After Skin Problems

Darkening left after eczema, burns, insect bites or skin injuries, which is common in darker skin.

Suitability

Is Pigmentation Treatment Right for You?

Most pigmentation can be improved, as long as the cause is clear and you can protect your skin every day.

Treatment may suit you if

  • You have brown or grey-brown patches on your cheeks, forehead or upper lip
  • Dark marks stay behind after pimples, eczema or injuries
  • You have sun spots or uneven tone from time spent in the sun
  • You are ready to use sunscreen every day and follow a routine for several months

See a doctor first, or wait, if

  • A spot is new, changing, itching or bleeding, or a dark spot is growing on your palm, sole or nail
  • You are pregnant or breastfeeding, because several creams and procedures are delayed
  • You have been using steroid or 'fairness' creams, which need to be stopped under a doctor's guidance
  • You have active acne, eczema or an infection on the area to be treated
  • You have taken isotretinoin recently or tend to form raised scars, which affects peel and laser plans

Our aim is to fade patches and marks and even out your own skin tone, not to change your natural skin colour.

Treatment Plan

How Pigmentation Treatment Works

Plans are built in layers: protection first, then creams, then procedures if they are needed.

01

Assessment

The doctor asks when the patches started, about pregnancy, pills, heat at work or home and the creams you have used, then examines your skin in good light. Photos are taken, with your consent, to compare progress.

02

Sun Protection & Routine

A broad-spectrum sunscreen of SPF 30 or higher, ideally a tinted one with iron oxides, is used every day and reapplied when you are outdoors, with a gentle cleanser and moisturiser.

03

Prescription Creams

Creams such as hydroquinone, azelaic acid or a short course of a triple combination cream are prescribed for a set period. Tranexamic acid tablets are considered only after checking your clotting risk.

04

Peels or Laser Toning

Superficial chemical peels every two to four weeks, after skin preparation, or laser toning for stubborn melasma, are added when creams alone are not enough.

05

Maintenance

Once patches fade, sunscreen and a gentler maintenance routine help keep them away, because melasma often comes back with sun, heat or hormonal changes.

Timeline

Pigmentation Treatment Timeline

Pigment fades slowly. Most people see results between three and twelve months.

W2

First Two to Four Weeks

Skin adjusts to the new routine and sunscreen; the first peel is planned if your skin is ready.

W8

Around Two Months

Acne marks often look lighter; the doctor reviews progress and adjusts creams.

M3

Three Months

Many people see a clear difference; creams such as hydroquinone are stopped or reduced as planned.

M6

Six Months

Melasma usually needs this long or longer; any course of peels or laser toning is completed.

Y1

Ongoing

Maintenance and sun protection continue; a flare in summer or pregnancy is treated early.

Medical Note: Results vary from person to person. This page is general information from Kezza Hair & Skin Clinic and is not a substitute for a consultation with a doctor.

Melasma: why it keeps coming back

Melasma is a long-term condition rather than a one-off problem. In a study of 1,001 people with melasma across ten Indian centres, 85% were women, heat from cooking fires or work was linked to more severe patches, only about one in five used sunscreen, and more than a quarter had used steroid or triple creams. Each of these points shapes treatment. Daily sunscreen, a hat and shade reduce the trigger; heat is reduced where possible; and steroid creams are stopped safely. Even with good treatment, melasma often returns in summer, in pregnancy or when sunscreen is skipped, so the plan includes what to do at the first sign of a flare.

Prescription creams: what they do and their limits

  • Hydroquinone is one of the most studied creams for melasma. It is used for a limited period, usually two to four months, and stopped if there is no benefit by three months. Long use of high strengths can cause a blue-black darkening called ochronosis, so it is not used open-endedly.
  • Triple combination cream (hydroquinone, a retinoid and a mild steroid) can clear or improve melasma in many people, but it is meant for short courses. The steroid can thin the skin and cause stretch marks and visible blood vessels if it is overused.
  • Azelaic acid, kojic acid, vitamin C and niacinamide are gentler options that are useful for maintenance and for sensitive skin.
  • Tranexamic acid tablets can help when other treatments have not worked. They are not suitable for people with clotting problems, a past blood clot, heart disease or a stroke, so they are prescribed only after a doctor checks your history, and melasma can return after stopping them.

Please do not buy steroid-containing creams for your face without a prescription. Fourteen topical steroids became prescription-only in India in 2018 because of misuse, and steroid damage to facial skin is much harder to treat than pigmentation.

Chemical peels and laser toning

Superficial chemical peels with glycolic, salicylic, lactic or mandelic acid loosen the outer layer of skin and help creams work. Indian guidelines consider superficial peels safe for Indian skin and do not recommend deep peels. Peels are usually spaced two to four weeks apart, after two to four weeks of skin preparation, and the strength is increased only as your skin tolerates it. Our guide to chemical peels for pigmentation explains the different acids.

Laser toning uses a low-energy Q-switched Nd:YAG laser over several sessions. Indian experts advise that laser should not be the first treatment for melasma, and studies report improvement ranging from about a fifth to three-quarters, with frequent relapse. Too many or too strong sessions can leave mottled light patches. For these reasons, laser toning is reserved for stubborn cases and always combined with sun protection and creams.

Pigmentation care for Indian skin

Medium and darker skin types make pigment easily, which is why they are more prone to melasma and to dark marks after acne or irritation. The same tendency means that aggressive treatment can backfire: a strong peel, a hot laser setting or a harsh scrub can cause new darkening. A safe plan starts gently, prepares the skin, increases strength slowly and treats irritation quickly. Your skin type, how easily you tan and how your skin has reacted to past treatments all guide the choice of creams, peels and settings.

Why patients choose Kezza for pigmentation care

  • Cause first: a doctor works out whether you have melasma, marks, sun spots or tanning before suggesting treatment.
  • Planned for your skin type: peel strength, laser settings and the gap between sessions are chosen to lower the risk of new dark marks.
  • Prescriptions with limits: creams such as hydroquinone and steroid combinations are used for set periods, with reviews.
  • Three clinics: Jaipur, Sikar and Ajmer, open 9 AM to 8 PM every day, so follow-up visits are easier to keep.
  • Clear costs: the plan, the number of sessions and the total cost are explained before you start.

What affects the cost of pigmentation treatment?

The cost depends on the type and extent of pigmentation, whether creams alone are enough, and how many peel or laser sessions are planned. Melasma usually needs a longer plan with maintenance, while a few sun spots or acne marks may need less. Your doctor explains the options and the total cost at your consultation.

FAQs

Frequently Asked Questions

Can melasma be cured permanently?
There is no cure for melasma, but it can be controlled. Patches usually fade with sun protection and treatment, and they often come back when treatment stops or after sun exposure, heat or hormonal changes. That is why a maintenance routine, especially daily sunscreen, continues after the patches have faded.
How long does pigmentation treatment take to work?
It is gradual. The American Academy of Dermatology says it usually takes between three and twelve months to see results. Acne marks often respond within a few months, while melasma and deeper pigment take longer.
Does pigmentation from pregnancy go away?
Melasma that starts in pregnancy often fades over several months after the baby is born or after stopping hormone medicines, but it can return in a later pregnancy or with sun exposure. During pregnancy, sunscreen is the main treatment, and creams and procedures are planned for after pregnancy and breastfeeding.
Which sunscreen is best for pigmentation?
A broad-spectrum sunscreen of SPF 30 or higher, reapplied about every two hours outdoors. Indian dermatology advice suggests SPF 50 with a high UVA (PA) rating. For melasma, a tinted sunscreen containing iron oxides also protects against visible light, which can worsen it in darker skin.
Is laser toning good for melasma?
It can help some people with stubborn melasma, but it is not a first treatment. Studies of laser toning use around six to ten sessions two weeks apart, with results that vary widely, and melasma often returns. Overtreatment can leave patches of lighter skin, so laser toning is used carefully, alongside creams and sun protection.
Can glutathione treat pigmentation?
Glutathione is widely promoted for skin lightening, but there is no reliable evidence that glutathione injections work, serious side effects have been reported, and the US Food and Drug Administration has not approved any injectable drug for skin lightening. It is not a treatment for melasma; sun protection and the treatments on this page have much better evidence.
Do acne marks fade on their own?
Mild dark marks often fade within six to twelve months, but deeper marks can take much longer. Sunscreen and treatment speed this up. Marks are flat; if the skin is pitted or raised, those are scars, which are treated differently on our acne scar treatment page.
Are skin-lightening or triple creams from the chemist safe?
Not without a doctor's advice. Many such creams contain strong steroids. Indian studies have found widespread misuse of steroid creams on the face, often as 'fairness' creams, causing thin, red, sensitive skin that is hard to treat. These creams are prescription-only in India, and a doctor decides whether, and for how long, they are safe to use.
